tip: Marcara is the simple pluperfect, a one-word literary form equal to tinha marcado (had marked). Rare in speech, common in writing.
Se (if) about the future uses the future subjunctive: se a chuva parar. For regular verbs the form looks identical to the infinitive.
Trouxer is the future subjunctive of trazer (to bring); its stem comes from the preterite trouxe, not the infinitive.
Vira here is the pluperfect of ver (had seen), a one-word had-form. Do not confuse it with virar, meaning to turn.
Put o before an adjective to turn it into a noun: o barato means the cheap thing or option.
Set off by commas mid-sentence, pois means therefore, not because. It is a formal connector in academic writing.
Cumpre plus an infinitive is an impersonal formal phrase: cumpre salientar means it should be pointed out.
